questions.question: For $Q(x)=x^{\top} Ax$ with $A$ symmetric $n\times n$ and the constraint set $Bx=0$ with $B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, which matrix is the bordered matrix $H$?

A quadratic form in three variables is restricted by $x_1+x_2=0$ and $2x_1+2x_2=0$. Why must these two equations be reduced before applying the bordered matrix test with an independent constraint matrix?
options: Their repeated coefficients make every $A$ singular.
They specify only one independent constraint.
They force the quadratic form to be definite.

questions.question: Let $Q(x)=x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2$ and impose $x_3=0$. For $B=(0,0,1)$ and $H=\begin{pmatrix}0&B\\B^{\top}&I_3\end{pmatrix}$, the relevant leading determinants are $\det(H_3)=0$ and $\det(H_4)=-1$. What follows for the restriction of $Q$ to $x_3=0$?
options: The zero determinant proves that the restriction is indefinite.
The zero determinant proves that the restriction is not positive definite.
The sign test fails, although the restriction is positive definite.
The sign test fails because the constraint row is redundant.

questions.question: If $A$ is positive definite on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\operatorname{rank}(B)=m<n$, what can be said about $Q(x)=x^{\top} Ax$ on $Bx=0$ without computing any minor?
options: Nothing until the bordered minors have been checked
It may fail to be positive, as constraints add directions
It is positive definite only if $B$ has orthonormal rows
It is positive definite, as $Q(x)>0$ for all $x\ne0$

questions.question: To test a quadratic form on the line spanned by $(2,1)$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, which constraint matrix $B$ in $Bx=0$ describes that line?

Let $1\le m<n$, let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be symmetric, and let $B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ have rank $m$. Set $H=\begin{pmatrix}0_m&B\\B^{\top}&A\end{pmatrix}$, and let $H_k$ be its leading $k\times k$ submatrix. Why does the bordered matrix test ignore the determinants for $k\le2m$?
options: They are always positive, so they carry no sign information.
They are independent of $A$, so they reveal no restricted curvature.
They involve only $A$, so they test the wrong subspace.
They always vanish, so they cannot provide any sign.

questions.question: For which values of $c$ does the bordered matrix test show that $Q(x)=x_1^2+cx_2^2$ is positive definite on $x_1+x_2=0$?

Let $Q_t(x)=x^{\top} A(t)x$ in four variables, with $A(t)$ symmetric, and impose one independent constraint $Bx=0$. Set $H(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&B\\B^{\top}&A(t)\end{pmatrix}$ and write $H_k(t)$ for its leading $k\times k$ submatrix. Suppose the leading determinants are $0,-4,t,1-t,t-1$, in order. For which real $t$ does the bordered sign test establish negative definiteness?
